nodes.Node: Robot learning problem formulation: observations, actions, policies
nodes.What it is: A policy is a function that turns sensor observations into robot commands. Choosing what the robot observes, what an action means, and how often it acts is part of the learning problem, not just an implementation detail.
nodes.Prerequisites: Python arrays; basic probability; robot joint and coordinate-frame vocabulary
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Observation histories help with hidden state; action units and control frequency must agree between data and deployment. Start with a small explicit interface before trying a generalist policy. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Offline inspection or a small Python example; no robot purchase needed.

nodes.What it is: A robot-learning toolchain stores episodes, trains policies, and replays their results. Formats such as LeRobotDataset and RLDS record observations and actions with timing and episode boundaries so different programs can use the same experience.
nodes.Prerequisites: Python; tables; video files; episode and timestep concepts
nodes.Frontier state 2026: LeRobotDataset v3 documents scalable storage; RLDS provides episodic interchange but its repository is archived. Conversions must preserve timestamps, action conventions, terminal flags and data licenses rather than just rename columns. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Hugging Face LeRobot; Google Research; ARISE Initiative
nodes._accessibility_reason: Offline inspection or a small Python example; no robot purchase needed.

nodes.What it is: Evaluation asks whether a policy completes a task on trials it did not train on. A useful test fixes success rules and reset conditions, counts failures, and separates familiar scenes from new objects, backgrounds or tasks.
nodes.Prerequisites: Basic statistics; train/test splits; safe experiment resets
nodes.Frontier state 2026: LIBERO and RoboCasa expose structured generalization tests, not a universal real-world score. Hold out episodes and environments, report uncertainty across seeds, and distinguish simulated success from physical reliability. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: LIBERO authors; RoboCasa authors; ARISE Initiative
nodes._accessibility_reason: Public code and simulation/replay permit a first demo; careful dataset controls still take work.

nodes.What it is: These policies generate a sequence of robot commands by gradually transforming noise into actions. Unlike averaging all demonstrations into one answer, a generative policy can represent several valid ways to solve the same scene.
nodes.Prerequisites: Imitation learning (behavior cloning); neural networks; conditional probability
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Diffusion Policy is a strong specialist reference; pi0 uses flow matching for general robot control. Denoising steps, action horizon and inference delay must be evaluated together; published success does not imply SO-101 compatibility. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Accessible reference code, but GPU/debugging and rigorous evaluation are significant barriers.

nodes.What it is: Action chunking predicts several future commands at once instead of one command at each camera frame. Tokenization converts continuous commands into symbols; FAST compresses an action sequence in frequency space rather than binning every value independently.
nodes.Prerequisites: Imitation learning (behavior cloning); time-series arrays; transformer basics
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ACT motivates chunked prediction and temporal ensembling; FAST addresses high-frequency action tokenization. Compression error, chunk length and feedback delay are different trade-offs and should be measured separately. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Stanford ACT authors; Physical Intelligence FAST authors
nodes._accessibility_reason: Public code and simulation/replay permit a first demo; careful dataset controls still take work.

nodes.What it is: A visual encoder turns camera images into feature vectors before a small policy chooses actions. Reusing an encoder trained on large image or video collections can reduce training work, but features that recognize objects may still miss details needed for precise control.
nodes.Prerequisites: Image tensors; neural network embeddings; supervised learning
nodes.Frontier state 2026: R3M, VC-1 and DINOv2 are complementary reference encoders rather than a 2026 ranking. CortexBench finds no universally dominant representation; frozen-feature and fine-tuned comparisons need matched data and control heads. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: R3M authors; Meta FAIR; CortexBench collaboration
nodes._accessibility_reason: Public code and simulation/replay permit a first demo; careful dataset controls still take work.

nodes.What it is: Offline reinforcement learning improves a policy using a fixed collection of past transitions and rewards, without exploring during training. Its main trap is trusting actions that look valuable to the model but are poorly covered by the recorded data.
nodes.Prerequisites: Reinforcement learning for robots; value functions; reward definitions
nodes.Frontier state 2026: CQL penalizes optimistic out-of-data values and IQL avoids evaluating unseen actions during value learning. Implementation and dataset changes can alter conclusions; use behavior cloning and matched splits as baselines before online transfer. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: UC Berkeley; CQL and IQL authors
nodes._accessibility_reason: Accessible reference code, but GPU/debugging and rigorous evaluation are significant barriers.

nodes.What it is: A reward tells a learning system which outcomes are desirable, but a convenient score may not match the real goal. Reward learning uses examples or feedback to estimate that score, while language and vision models can help propose or judge rewards.
nodes.Prerequisites: Reinforcement learning for robots; validation labels; false positives
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Eureka generates reward code; D&A (2026 preprint) separates video description from progress assessment to address VLM reward bias. Neither makes an unsupervised success judge trustworthy by default; test failed and ambiguous episodes independently. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Accessible reference code, but GPU/debugging and rigorous evaluation are significant barriers.

nodes.What it is: A policy can drift into situations missing from its demonstrations. Interactive imitation asks a person for correct actions in those visited states, then adds the corrections to training instead of repeatedly collecting only perfect expert runs.
nodes.Prerequisites: Imitation learning (behavior cloning); safe override interface; dataset versioning
nodes.Frontier state 2026: DAgger explains distribution shift and iterative expert labeling. Robotic Data Inoculation (2026 preprint) explores human correction under learned perturbations; treat it as research, not permission for unsafe online exploration. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: DAgger authors; UC Berkeley Data Inoculation authors
nodes._accessibility_reason: Public code and simulation/replay permit a first demo; careful dataset controls still take work.

nodes.What it is: Augmentation changes training examples while keeping their intended action or outcome valid. Synthetic demonstration generation goes further by adapting trajectories to new scenes, so a few human demonstrations can cover more starting conditions.
nodes.Prerequisites: Imitation learning (behavior cloning); coordinate transforms; simulator resets
nodes.Frontier state 2026: MimicGen adapts object-relative trajectory segments; Augmentron (2026 preprint) targets temporal and multi-camera visual consistency. Synthetic volume is not equivalent to independent coverage: track failed generations and test on untouched scenes. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Public code and simulation/replay permit a first demo; careful dataset controls still take work.

nodes.What it is: Fine-tuning updates a pretrained policy using demonstrations from a new task or robot. Small adapters such as LoRA can reduce the number of trainable weights, but the action interface, normalization and camera setup must still match the target system.
nodes.Prerequisites: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs); dataset splits; GPU training basics
nodes.Frontier state 2026: openpi documents policy adaptation and LoRA configurations; LeRobot documents SmolVLA and NVIDIA releases GR00T models. Compare adapter and full tuning under equal data budgets; support for one embodiment is not evidence for another. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Accessible reference code, but GPU/debugging and rigorous evaluation are significant barriers.

nodes.What it is: A learned policy may need longer to compute than the robot can safely wait between commands. Scheduling overlaps computation with execution and decides how to join action chunks without sending stale or discontinuous commands.
nodes.Prerequisites: Action chunking; timestamps; queues; safe command limits
nodes.Frontier state 2026: RTC and LeRobot asynchronous inference address policy latency at the action queue level, not embedded hardware design. A 2026 control-aware scheduling preprint extends this direction; quantization is only an optional hypothesis until accuracy and timing are measured. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Physical Intelligence; Hugging Face; control-aware command generation authors
nodes._accessibility_reason: Accessible reference code, but GPU/debugging and rigorous evaluation are significant barriers.

nodes.What it is: A language or vision-language model can choose a sequence of existing robot skills or write code that calls them. This is a high-level decision layer, not a replacement for a controller that knows how to move safely.
nodes.Prerequisites: Planning basics; API contracts; sandboxing; robot skill interfaces
nodes.Frontier state 2026: SayCan grounds skill selection in feasibility and Code as Policies composes perception/action APIs. This node studies grounding and executable contracts, not another generic long-horizon manipulation pipeline; generated code must never bypass a safety gate. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Google Research; Code as Policies and SayCan authors
nodes._accessibility_reason: Accessible reference code, but GPU/debugging and rigorous evaluation are significant barriers.

nodes.What it is: Cross-embodiment learning shares experience between robots with different bodies, sensors or command spaces. The challenge is deciding what can transfer without pretending that two robots have identical joints, reach or capabilities.
nodes.Prerequisites: Robot datasets & benchmarks; action spaces; normalization; multi-task learning
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Open X-Embodiment/RT-X demonstrates shared-data benefits; CrossFormer handles heterogeneous inputs and action heads. Transfer must be tested on held-out embodiments, not just held-out episodes from a robot seen during training. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Open X-Embodiment collaboration; UC Berkeley; CMU
nodes._accessibility_reason: Multi-task data, compute and controlled experiments make a credible result a multi-month effort.

nodes.What it is: Self-improvement alternates collecting experience and updating a policy instead of freezing it after one training run. Continual learning additionally asks whether new skills can be acquired without erasing older ones.
nodes.Prerequisites: Offline reinforcement learning; evaluation; replay buffers; safe rollback
nodes.Frontier state 2026: RoboCat demonstrates an iterative self-generated-data loop; RLPD combines prior data with online reinforcement learning. These are reference ingredients, not proof of unattended lifelong operation; gate each update on retained-skill tests and keep human-approved rollback. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Google DeepMind; UC Berkeley RLPD authors
nodes._accessibility_reason: Multi-task data, compute and controlled experiments make a credible result a multi-month effort.

nodes.Node: Failure detection & uncertainty for learned policies
nodes.What it is: A failure monitor estimates whether execution is going wrong and decides when to stop or ask for help. Uncertainty is useful only if it predicts real mistakes; a confident model can still be wrong in a new scene.
nodes.Prerequisites: Probability; calibration; held-out data; safe stopping interface
nodes.Frontier state 2026: KnowNo calibrates ambiguity in language planners, not arbitrary low-level robot failures. Use separate action-level monitors and test distribution shift; conformal guarantees require their statistical assumptions and do not certify physical safety. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive November 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Accessible reference code, but GPU/debugging and rigorous evaluation are significant barriers.

top3.justification: High accessibility: offline action compression produces an immediately understandable trajectory movie. FAST and ACT connect directly to the open robot-learning ecosystem without requiring a new robot; measure token savings rather than assuming a better controller.

MimicGen produces filmable demonstrations from a small seed set and makes dataset coverage tangible. Simulation-first work has no incremental robot cost and tests whether a low-cost learning wedge can scale its data; invalid generations must remain in the audit.

Queue visualizations and delay-injected simulations are cheap, compelling and directly relevant to practical LeRobot deployment. A focused systems contribution fits software students, while physical extension waits for measured timing and safe stopping.
